Definition: from G1658; to liberate, i.e. (figuratively) to exempt (from moral, ceremonial or mortal liability):--deliver, make free.
BiblicalUsage: The word eleutheróō carries the sense of deliver, make free. In John 8:32, the text says "and the truth shall make you free." In John 8:36, the text says "If the Son therefore shall make you free."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: eleutheróō tells me that freedom in Christ is real freedom: not doing whatever we please, but being set free to live as God made us to live. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
